Class RegexSyntaxHighlighter

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.widgets.syntax.RegexSyntaxHighlighter
All Implemented Interfaces:
SyntaxHighlighter
public final class RegexSyntaxHighlighter extends Object implements SyntaxHighlighter
The built-in SyntaxHighlighter. It tokenizes a snippet using an ordered set of regex Grammars (inspired by highlight.js) and applies the configured SyntaxTheme to turn each TokenType into a Style. Every source line becomes a single Line holding one Span per token, so widths, clipping and wrapping keep working unchanged.

Use defaults() for an instance covering the popular built-in languages, or builder() to start from those and add/mark languages missing from the defaults.

Multi-line constructs (block comments, triple-quoted strings) are handled by the grammar's Grammar.Rule.multiline(TokenType, String, String) rules and are emitted as a single token spanning the newlines that separate them, exactly like a highlight.js beginsWith/endsWith pair.

    • highlight

      public List<Line> highlight(String code, String language, Style base, SyntaxTheme theme)
      Description copied from interface: SyntaxHighlighter
      Highlights code, which must contain only the code lines, into one Line per source line. The returned lines may carry multiple spans with distinct styles; texat not matched by a grammar keeps the given base style.
      Specified by:
      highlight in interface SyntaxHighlighter
      Parameters:
      code - the raw snippet, possibly multi-line
      language - the fenced-block info string (e.g. java), or the empty string when unknown; may be null
      base - the style applied to non-tokenized text (generally the code-block style)
      theme - the palette mapping token types to styles
      Returns:
      one styled Line per source line; never null
